correctness.rationale: With bipartition-oriented tree edges, K=B^T B is positive definite and (Kd)_uv=S_u+S_v. Connectedness forces constant signed sums s on A and t on B, |A|s=|B|t=Σ_e d_e; for c=s+t>0 these are positive. The unique solution to Jd=f on a tree is exactly the cut flow D_e, proving iff |D_e|=1. For mixed d, the invariant circle p+u1 satisfies u↦u+(s+t)h sin(u); positive definite KΔ is similar to the symmetric K^(1/2)ΔK^(1/2), with positive/negative inertia determined by d. Its positive subspace E+ is unstable at p and stable at p+π1, coincides along the heteroclinic, and is proper, thus violates transversality. If unequal s,t with r>=1 negative, q=n-1-2r<=n-3 is divisible by lcm(|A|,|B|), excluding n<=8. At n=9 only (|A|,|B|)=(6,3), (s,t)=(1,2), r=1 survive; parity and degree counts force unique signed tree. Constructive b odd, k>=2 family meets sums and extends indefinitely. Independent 32 checks of cuts, nine-vertex construction, lcm exclusions support analytic proof; no inference of arbitrary Morse–Smale behavior from criterion failure.

originality.rationale: The exact invariant-line nontransversality mechanism and equal vertexwise signed-sum one case are established by Buescu–D’Aniello–Oliveira (arXiv:2610.10993v1) Propositions 5.11–5.12, including a six-vertex example. The present theorem explicitly restricts sharp nine-vertex minimality to unequal incident sums and derives the exact arbitrary tree cut criterion, uniqueness, and a new unbalanced family. Inspected complete HTML §5.4 does not state the unequal-class sharp onset, although the prior argument suggests extension. Qualified novelty for this exact signed-flow classification, not the underlying heteroclinic idea.
residual_risks: The signed incidence cut condition is a standard flow identity; earlier signed-flow literature may have its exact tree classification.
The heteroclinic tangent mechanism is directly adapted from the published balanced case; no claim of invention of that general method.
Failure of the cut criterion does not establish Morse–Smale dynamics; other obstructions may exist.

value.rationale: A precise combinatorial criterion and sharp minimal example for a physically motivated nontransversality obstruction, extending the known balanced-sign mechanism to unequal bipartition classes. The nine-vertex threshold and unique signed topology are natural exact structural facts.

final_claim: For a finite tree T bipartition A∪B, positive integer target incident sums s,t with |A|s=|B|t, the unique real cut-flow d_e=s|A∩C_e|-t|B∩C_e| yields a ±1 sign vector iff every |d_e|=1. Mixed signs give Kd=(s+t)1 and a nontransverse heteroclinic invariant-circle arc for every 0<h<1/lambda_max(K). With unequal s≠t the smallest such signed tree has nine vertices, unique up to isomorphism, and arbitrarily large unequal-class families exist.
limitations: Finite unweighted trees, edge phase torus, positive strict step 0<h<1/lambda_max(K), non-Morse–Smale diagonal mechanism only; not an all-tree classification of every heteroclinic defect.
